chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf who said:

Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me in Khurasan while I was complaining about my eyes, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I point you to something that if you do it, your eye will not complain?' So I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Take from your nails every Thursday.' He said: 'So I did it, and I did not complain about my eye until the day I informed you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended day for clipping nails according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of the Imams by linking physical hygiene to spiritual well-being, specifically prescribing nail clipping on Thursdays as a remedy for eye ailments. In Shia scholarly tradition, this incident is often cited to support the virtue of maintaining cleanliness (taharah) as an act of worship, with Thursday being a significant day for preparing for Friday prayers. The cure of the companion’s eye serves as a tangible example of how following the Imam’s guidance in daily habits can yield both physical and spiritual benefits.
